planted_anomaly_detections.note: the frozen 37/50/31 budget lives in CUSTOMER_MASTER and INVOICE_LINE, which belong to other wave 1 batches; none of this batch's three tables carries a budgeted anomaly, and none was found

unverified_paths: notifications.kind is decoded through CODES NOTIF_KIND, so the source integer and the target string never compare raw. It is graded by tier 4 parity operations (notifications_kind_decode, notifications_kind_counts) that decode on the SQL side, not by tier 3.

The harness ships no yn_to_bool, csv_split_trim or parse_date_string rule. None of the three fields in this batch needs one, so no field here is left ungraded by that gap; the rules stay raised as profile feedback in .migration/canonicalization.json and the harness was not patched.

audit_log is empty at source (0 rows), so its field grading and its TTL index are structurally exercised but not value-exercised. The 90-day TTL on loggedAt was created and read back, but no document has ever been old enough for the TTL monitor to remove, so expiry itself is untested.

notifications holds a single row, so the unique index on (tenantId, kind, sentAt) is proven unique over a population of one, not under a collision. The reload proof shows it does not duplicate on a second load.

NOTIFICATIONS.SENT_AT is an Oracle TIMESTAMP with microsecond resolution and uq_notifications compares all six fractional digits, while canonicalization truncates to milliseconds. Two same-tenant, same-kind rows less than a millisecond apart would therefore collide on the mapped unique index. Checked against the source: zero such groups exist, so nothing is lost here. The mapping spec fixes both the millisecond truncation and the index, so closing the gap is a contract change, not a loader change.
Money parity for credit_notes is graded on values that are whole units (5, 25, 30, 55), so the 0.01 money-aggregate tolerance is not exercised by a fractional cent.

The repo self-check asks for an ow_tp / ow-tp- namespace prefix. The engagement intake fixes the target database as ow_billing_migration, so the prefix rule is deliberately not met; .migration/allowed_targets.json is the control instead.
Scale is the demo estate on an Atlas M0 cluster. Nothing here is a statement about production volumes.

The load reads Oracle in one read-only transaction, so it is snapshot-consistent; it is not serialised against a second concurrent loader, which the wave manifest's disjoint write targets prevent rather than the code.

tier3_keyed_diffs.mode: full_diff on every collection; no sampling

source_access: SELECT/WITH only, in a single read-only transaction; no DDL or DML against OW_BILLING
